name: deployment
description: Decides how an application actually ships, then writes the files for it — but asks first and never assumes a container. Its entry-point skill asks what ships, who uses it, and what it does to data (facts a non-infrastructure person can answer), maps those onto a deployment shape (static hosting / PaaS / container on a managed runtime / serverless / container-plus-orchestrator / VM) with the reasoning for why that shape and not the others, then presents a deployment plan and stops for confirmation before creating a Dockerfile, a pipeline file, or an environment. Container authoring is skipped entirely for a project that should deploy statically. Covers multi-stage image builds, minimal non-root runtime bases, layer-cache ordering, .dockerignore, signal handling, health probes, immutable commit-SHA tags, and a local-dev compose file; plus CI/CD pipelines for whichever platform the project actually uses (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, Cloud Build, or Jenkins) with stage gates, OIDC federation instead of long-lived keys, build-once-then-promote across dev/staging/prod, canary rollout, and a tested rollback path. Wires into a sibling api-contract plugin's existing OpenAPI diff gate and a sibling e2e-testing plugin's run-against-deployed-staging posture rather than reinventing either. Also owns the dev/staging/prod contract — what must differ between environments and what must not (the artifact, the runtime, and the config keys, so a missing one fails in dev rather than production), where secrets actually live and the three places they leak, config validated at startup, expand-then-contract migrations so code can still roll back past a schema change, and why production data never moves downward — plus a severity-grouped review checklist for a deployment that already exists, with an explicit list of things not to flag. Recommendations are grounded in Google's published guidance — the Cloud Architecture Framework pillars, their container build practices, the SRE Book/Workbook, DORA's four key metrics, and SLSA supply-chain practice. Use when the user says things like "how should we deploy this", "do we need Docker", "should we containerize", "write a Dockerfile", "set up CI/CD", "automate the deploy", "how do we roll back", "set up staging", "how do we manage secrets", "dev vs prod config", "review our deployment", or "we keep breaking prod".
